title: conditioning-patterns-scratchbook
content:
Personal scratchbook for prompt-conditioning experiments (very rough).

Goal: build a small library of conditioning patterns that are robust across model variants (ggml/quantized, float32 hosted) and degrade gracefully with token limits. Want to capture: positive anchors, negative anchors, role-priming, example ordering heuristics, and a tiny auto-selection algorithm for few-shot sets.

Quick notes / hypotheses:
- Positive anchors (short clarifying sentences before a request) reduce hallucination on knowledge-limited tasks. e.g., "Based only on the content provided below, answer concisely. Do not use outside knowledge." seems to drop hallucinated facts by ~15% in preliminary runs.
- Negative anchors (explicit "do not" statements) are brittle: they often get ignored unless repeated near the end of the prompt. Use them sparingly.
- Persona priming helps style consistency but increases verbosity; append a "length: concise" constraint to counteract.
- Ordering examples: put the shortest, clearest example first, then a tricky borderline example, then the target. This seems to prime the model for the minimal transform and then show exception handling.
- Dynamic shot selection: choose examples whose edit-distance to the input is within 30–70 percentile of the historical sample distribution. Too-close examples cause parroting; too-distant cause noisy generalization.

Mini templates (copyable):
1) Constrained extraction (for SRO/TOS scraping)
"""
Context: <DOCUMENT_TEXT>
Instruction: Extract the following fields in JSON. Only include the keys that appear in the text. Respond with valid JSON and no additional commentary.
Fields: {title, effective_date, jurisdiction, parties}
Example:
Input: "Purchase Agreement between Foo Inc. and Bar LLC, effective Jan 1 2021, jurisdiction: CA"
Output: {"title": "Purchase Agreement", "effective_date": "2021-01-01", "jurisdiction": "CA", "parties": ["Foo Inc.", "Bar LLC"]}
"""
Notes: include the explicit schema line and "Respond with valid JSON" to reduce prose. Test with truncated documents to measure robustness.

2) Few-shot paraphrase set (for embeddings rerank + generation)
- Shot A (short): Q: "How to reset password?" A: "Click Forgot password and follow the email link."
- Shot B (edge): Q: "I can't log in after SSO migration" A: "Reach out to IT; check account mapping and try the SSO link again."
- Prompt framing: "You are a friendly support assistant. Given a user question, produce a 1-2 sentence helpful answer that includes the next step and a troubleshooting tip."

3) Rewriting/code-simplify template
"""
Task: Simplify the following Python function while preserving behavior and adding inline comments. Return only the simplified code block.
Input:
<code>def f(a):
    res = []
    for x in a:
        if x % 2 == 0:
            res.append(x*2)
    return res
Output:
"""
Heuristic: require the model to output a single fenced code block beginning with ```python. If it outputs anything else, feed into a small validator script that rejects non-code.

Failure cases observed (notes from runs on hosted v2 / local quantized):
- Hallucinated dates in extraction when anchor not explicit; use explicit schema + example to mitigate.
- Negations were flipped in ~7% of classification prompts for short inputs. Suspect attention to token boundaries when quantized kernels drop precision. Add a redundancy check: append a simple yes/no verification question and expect Json {"ok": true}.
- Truncation: longest-shot concat causes last example to be cut off -> model reuses previous example pattern. Mitigation: elastic shot insertion and end-of-prompt sentinel token (e.g., "<END_OF_EXAMPLES>").
- Overfitting to few-shot wording: observed parroting of shot-specific phrases. Randomize phrasing of examples programmatically.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Variable: anchor type (none / positive / negative / both) x example order (short-first / long-first / mixed) x model variant (hosted-1 / hosted-2 / local-q4_0 / local-q8_1) x truncation simulated (0/25/50 tokens trimmed)
- Metrics: exact-match extraction, BLEU/paraphrase divergence, hallucination-rate (manual labeling on sample of 200), latency (ms/token), cost (tokens).
- Run plan: run seed=42 x 3 seeds for statistical stability; randomize example phrasing using small synonym map.

Small few-shot sets (for quick A/B):
Task: classify tone of short customer messages (positive / neutral / frustrated).
Shots:
- S1: "Thanks for the quick help!" -> positive
- S2: "Ok I tried that, still not working, anyone?" -> frustrated
- S3: "The update looks fine, no issues seen." -> neutral
Prompt core: "Label the tone as one of: positive, neutral, frustrated. Output only the label. If ambiguous, prefer neutral."
Edge: when messages mention expletives or all caps, model sometimes outputs multi-word justification. Add strict instruction: "Output only one of: positive|neutral|frustrated".

Notes-to-self (TODOs):
- Add small JS harness to randomize example phrasing and reorder automatically; integrate into existing prompt-benchmarks repo (see linked PR).
- Automate the verification JSON wrapper that re-queries model for {"ok":true} and score only accepted outputs. Keep failure logs for retraining few-shot set.
- Test negative-anchor repetition (place near top and repeated before examples) to see breakpoints where model respects it.
- Try 'contrastive few-shot' where each shot shows a positive and a negative answer for same input — hypothesize stronger discrimination for binary tasks.

Loose brainstorm items:
- Idea: meta-instruction line that says "If you are going to hallucinate, say \"I don't know\"" may trigger guardrails. But models sometimes still fabricate. Consider adding a calibrated probability prompt: "If confidence < 60%, answer 'unknown'" — need to translate confidence into model behavior; maybe use bidirectional check with a verifier model.
- Idea: small chain-of-evidence step: after the main output, ask model to list up to 3 tokens/phrases that were the basis of the decision (cheap interpretability). Might fail under toxicity tasks.

Quick log of recent runs (manual copy):
- 2026-02-10 hosted-v2, anchor=positive, trunc=25 -> extraction EM 0.82, hallucination 0.06
- 2026-02-14 local-q4_0, anchor=none, trunc=0 -> extraction EM 0.68, hallucination 0.14 (note: q4_0 seems to hallucinate more on small schemas)
- 2026-02-21 hosted-v1, contrastive-shots -> classification accuracy +.05 vs baseline

References / links:
- Related Linear ticket: DIFF-482 (linked above)
- Small validator script in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/examples/validator/check_json.py
- Slack thread: #prompt-hunches (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABCDE3)

End-of-scratchbook checklist (short):
- [ ] JS harness + randomizer
- [ ] Verification wrapper + log archive
- [ ] Run full matrix on hosted-2 and local-q8_1
- [ ] Publish short internal note + recommended templates for SRE and CS teams

Notes to future-me: keep this file as the "experimental home" for conditioning patterns. When a pattern reliably improves EM/hallucination, copy to a canonical template file under shared_drives/product/hosted-api/prompt-templates/ with minimal comments for engineers.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the negative-anchor failure a precision loss introduced by quantization or a general attention phenomenon? Need ablation with identical seeds across hosts.
- Can we design a tiny verifier policy that uses model logprobs to estimate confidence reliably across quantized kernels?

Random scratch lines:
- "short-first then edge then target" seems to beat random order in 6/8 cases.
- sentinel token = <END_OF_EXAMPLES> works but increases token usage; maybe replace with a short ASCII marker.
- when in doubt, require strict JSON output and validate post-hoc.

-- Maya
